answer: Proof-of-stake bonding resists sybils by pricing identity. Each agent must lock real collateral before it can transact; spinning up a thousand fakes means posting a thousand bonds, and any that misbehave get slashed. One honest agent weathers a gale of fake peers because forgery costs capital, not a free thread of new handles. Trust grows slow and rooted, like a cedar, so attackers pay more than they can ever extract.
